title: Engineers Leadership Weekly Signal — Sprint Log & Cross-Team Notes 2028-09-05
content:
Purpose
Quick cross-team sync to surface sprint risks, major decisions, and unblock requests for platform engineering and adjacent teams (serving-runtime, observability, private-deployments). This doc is intentionally lightweight: notes + actions.

Attendees
Aditi Rao (owner) — platform engineering, Jonas Kim — serving-runtime, Priya Patel — observability, Evan Morales — private-deployments, Sofia Nguyen — release eng, Chen Li — infra, + 8 engineers on call (see Slack thread #lead-signal).

Agenda (30 min)
1) Quick metrics snapshot (2 min)
2) Sprint highlights & risks (10 min)
3) Cross-team dependencies and escalations (10 min)
4) Decisions & owners (5 min)

1) Quick metrics snapshot
- API p99 latency (hosted): 48 ms for short-text gen; target 40 ms (regression traced to LRU cache thrashing; more below).
- Dedicated cluster throughput: sustained at 86% of target on A100 pools; shortfall due to two capacity nodes stuck in maintenance.
- Error budget burn last 7 days: 1.8% (on 2.5% monthly allowance).
- On-call paging events: 3 for model load failures (serving-runtime), 1 for KMS key rotation anomaly (private-deployments).

2) Sprint highlights & risks
A) Serving-runtime: kernel selection improvement landed in feature branch; early perf shows 6–9% token throughput gain for MPT-style models. Risk: one micro-optimization (tensor reorder) increases peak GPU memory by ~4% causing OOMs in low-capacity tests. Workaround: conservative kernel selection for 2.7B variants until memory regression is fully characterized. Owner: Jonas. Jira: JIRA-PLAT-2147.

B) Caching: adaptive prefix cache prototype (platform cache team) is running in canary for a single high-volume customer. Early telemetry shows 22% token reduction and 14% downstream latency improvement. Next step: validate correctness against API-level dedupes & tool-calls (edge cases with function-calling preserved). Risk: cache staleness on pinned-version model rollouts. Owner: Aditi / Chen. Confluence: perf-budgeting doc.

C) Dedicated capacity: two nodes in eu-west remained in 'maintenance' due to firmware mismatch from vendor update; replacement windows scheduled for 9/7. Impact: temporary capacity restriction for EU customers using reserved pools. Mitigation: short-term routing to secondary region and auto-scaling of burstable pool. Owner: Chen.

D) Observability: rollout of token-level cost dashboards to product routes is 70% complete. Known gap: embedding route cost attribution for batched vs single requests is inconsistent. Requesting ETA from observability infra owners for remaining instrumentation. Owner: Priya.

E) Private deployments: 0.9.1 private agent released to pilot customers; one pilot reported HSM integration latency spike during initial bootstrap (timeout handled but noisy). Action: lower HSM client retry backoff and add more verbose telemetry for first-boot path. Owner: Evan.

3) Cross-team dependencies and escalations
- Model on-boarding cadence vs rollout safety: Research/Applied ML plans to push two new quantized variants next week. Requirement: serving-runtime must vet memory/runtime behavior on dedicated pools before open rollout. Blocker: serving-runtime needs 2 more dedicated test GPUs scheduled for 9/6–9/10. Action: Chen to provision or approve time on dev-gpu bank.

- Release window overlap: Release eng (Sofia) flagged that platform and runtime have overlapping cut windows on 9/12. Proposed mitigation: move runtime risky changes to 9/15 window to avoid combined risk. Decision deferred until code freeze triage tomorrow.

- SLO alert fatigue: Observability flagged noisy alerts tied to transient cache thrash. Proposed: add a 3-minute suppression window for that class of alerts and instrumented rate limiter. Action: Priya + Aditi to draft suppression rules by EOD 9/05.

- Compliance audit: Security requests audit logs for private deployments for last quarter. Private-deployments needs signed timeline; CS for affected customers must be notified. Action: Evan to surface ETA (target 9/10) and notify customer success.

4) Decisions & owners
- Delay kernel micro-optimization rollout for MPT 2.7B by default. Enforce opt-in flag for now. Owner: Jonas. Deadline: 2028-09-08.
- Proceed with broader prefix cache rollout to 20% of production after validating function-calling correctness in canary. Owner: Aditi. Deadline: 2028-09-12.
- Provision 2 additional GPUs to serving-runtime test bank (or approve time on dev-gpu bank). Owner: Chen. Deadline: 2028-09-06.
- Implement 3-minute suppression rule for cache-thrash alert class; add instrumentation markers. Owner: Priya + Aditi. Deadline: 2028-09-05 (draft) and 2028-09-09 (apply).
- Notify pilot customers about HSM bootstrap telemetry improvement and schedule fix release (0.9.2). Owner: Evan. Deadline: 2028-09-08.

Action items (tracked)
- Jonas: Add opt-in flag + internal doc describing memory tradeoffs (JIRA: JIRA-PLAT-2147) — due 9/08.
- Chen: Approve/provision GPUs for serving-runtime test bank — due 9/06.
- Aditi: Run additional correctness test on prefix-cache for function-calling edge cases; update canary checklist — due 9/09.
- Priya: Produce draft suppression rules and instrumentation tickets — draft due 9/05, rollout 9/09.
- Evan: Prepare 0.9.2 release note and customer pilot message re: HSM fix — due 9/08.
- Sofia: Re-evaluate release calendar, propose shift for runtime risky changes if needed — due 9/06.

Open questions / parking lot
- Should prefix cache support pinned-version exceptions explicitly in the cache layer? (parking for HLD discussion)
- Longer-term: can kernel selection be gated by a lightweight memory estimator before selecting higher-memory kernels? (investigate as backlog spike).

Notes from the floor (brief)
- Jonas: observed a pattern where low-sequence inference (<=8 tokens) had worse p99 than expected — likely an interaction between micro-batching and new kernel path.
- Chen: vendor has agreed to expedite firmware patch; timeline contingent on remote reboots during night window.
- Priya: embedding cost attribution inconsistency likely due to older batching shim in a subset of services — will route to that team for patch.

Next meeting & cadence
- Standing leadership weekly: Wednesdays 09:30 PT (30 min). Next: 2028-09-12. Smaller triage for release overlap: tomorrow 2028-09-06 16:00 PT (Sofia, Jonas, Chen, Aditi).

Appendix / references
- Canary checklist snapshot (short): smoke inference, function-call tests, KV cache warmup, telemetry sanity checks.
- Related tickets: JIRA-PLAT-2147 (kernel mem regression), JIRA-PLAT-2199 (prefix cache canary), JIRA-PLAT-2203 (observability batching shim).

Quick retrospective comment
- Positive: cross-team response to canary telemetry was fast; we validated token savings quickly.
- Improve: ensure release windows are centrally visible in the calendar to avoid overlap and last-minute shifts.

If anything is missing or mis-attributed, reply in the Slack thread #lead-signal or update this doc directly.
